title.narrative: WASH lifesaving assistance to IDPs from protracted conflict and cyclone-affected areas in Rakhine State

description.narrative: ltpgtModification Request (MR): The multisectoral humanitarian crisis in Myanmar remains complex and severe, compounded by pre-existing poverty, current political crisis, economic breakdown, and recent natural disaster. More than two years after the military coup, the conflict nationwide is still ongoing with 3,093,700 people displaced, including 2,804,700 displaced after the coup in February 2021, of whom 49% are children and 51% are women and girls (UNHCR, June 2024). In Pauktaw (PKT) and Sittwe (STW) townships, hundreds of thousands of Internally Displaced People (IDPs) are living in protracted displacement sites, confined in overcrowded camps with extreme limitations to access basic services and livelihoods and relying exclusively on external assistance. On 14th of May 2023, Cyclone Mocha left a trail of devastation on the coast of Myanmar, greatly exacerbating the existing needs. In this context of underfunded humanitarian assistance despite rising needs, the proposed project has been designed to address both the protracted crisis needs and the compounded needs created by Cyclone Mocha. It aims at recovering essential WASH services in PKT and STW and improving their sustainability through WASH assistance, contributing to maintain populations’ safety and dignity.lt/pgtltpgtHowever, since the beginning of the project, the security, political and socio-economic context in Rakhine has drastically deteriorated, marked by a recent spike in fighting, underlying inter-communal tensions and heavily restricted access to affected areas. The resumption of clashes between the Arakan Army (AA) and the Myanmar Armed Forces (MAF) in November 2023 worsened the already dire humanitarian situation and added further complications to critical humanitarian access challenges. The clashes have driven over 321,696 persons into displacement, while indiscriminate artillery shelling and bombing continued to harm civilians and destroy properties and infrastructure. Transportation means have remained suspended by the de facto authorities since November, leading to impossible access to camps, shortages of essential commodities and materials, and a sharp increase in prices. Additionally, phone and internet connections have been shut down since January 2024, and there is therefore currently no operational bank in STW township. Electricity cuts, continuous raids by MAF on villages, arbitrary arrests, and forced recruitment, as well as the National Military Service Law, have raised additional concerns among SI teams Despite significant efforts to maintain the implementation of activities to the best of its capacity, the closure of checkpoints, total lack of access to Pauktaw, shortage of available materials in the markets, and random searches of individuals by MAF in camps have inevitably impacted SI’s ability to execute as planned. This project review aims to adapt the initially planned activities to the changing context in Rakhine and deliver based on realistic opportunities. lt/pgtltpgtWhile the key objective of the project remains to provide safe and equitable access to improved WASH services for the entire population, some activities planned as part of the two complementary outcomes require adjustments considering feasibility constraints. Under Outcome 1, SI will strive to maintain essential lifesaving activities for 23,606 individuals in Pauktaw camps, ensuring access to safe and functional latrines and sludge treatment, while adjusting the other activities considering the availability of materials in camps. As part of Outcome 2, SI proposes to use the available budget from cancelled activities in Pauktaw to respond to the high needs in terms of latrine upgrade and improved access to sanitation for 51,724 IDPs in Sittwe. The proposed adjustments would allow to maximize project’s impact and address prevailing humanitarian needs of 75,330 individuals in cyclone-affected locations of 11 Sittwe camps and 4 protracted IDP camps in Pauktaw, instead of 60,796 initially targeted.ltbrgtlt/pgt
